MORIZ STUDIO / VISUAL RESEARCH10 OCTOBER 2026 · 20 REFERENCES

About me.
Twenty ways to introduce yourself.

Real portfolio pages pairing imagery with a personal description. Each example includes a saved screenshot, the writing approach, and one practical idea to borrow.

All 20 references were captured from live pages and visually inspected. The set includes dedicated About pages, a homepage introduction, and a homepage About section. Images are embedded in this file for offline viewing. The notes below are design judgments, not measured conversion results.

Three directions worth exploring for Moriz

01 / Clear and personal

One distinctive portrait, a short introduction, and concrete evidence of what you do. The most direct starting point for a concise homepage section.

Study Mindy Nguyen, Seán Halpin, and Adham Dannaway.

02 / Editorial and expressive

Use image scale, asymmetry, and confident typography to communicate taste. Keep the paragraph short enough to read at a glance.

Study Dennis Snellenberg, Lu Yu, and Tobias van Schneider.

03 / A recognizable character

Use an original illustrated portrait or avatar, supported by a clear role and a specific personal detail. The illustration should feel like the person.

Study Robb Owen and Aarron Walter.

A practical starting point

For Moriz’s homepage, I would start with Mindy’s clarity, Dennis’s asymmetry, and Seán’s portrait treatment. Keep the section focused on the person, the combination of research, design, and development, and one detail that makes the introduction memorable.

  1. A short heading that says who you are.
  2. Two or three sentences linking your experience to how you help clients.
  3. One authentic portrait or original illustrated likeness.
  4. One concrete supporting detail about your approach or background.
  5. A clear next step toward your work or a conversation.

This is a proposed direction for review. Actual biography, professional claims, and imagery should come from you.

Method and limits. Research and capture date: 10 October 2026. Screenshots show desktop compositions at a 1440px browser width, with taller captures for some sections. Several captures show a subsection rather than the top of the page. Sites may change. Mobile behavior, accessibility compliance, animation quality, and conversion performance were not audited. All writing in the notes is paraphrased; screenshot content and imagery belong to their respective portfolio owners.

Source notes. Robb Owen is a homepage introduction. Sarah Drasner is a homepage About section. Andrew Neyer combines a portfolio and product shop. Devon Stank’s selected crop uses environmental imagery. The three Alice Lee references are separate designers, identified by name and domain on their cards. Broken, missing, and unrelated pages found during the search were excluded.
